**2026-11-08 — Engine sets browser, slice 1a–1b (branch `feature/engine-sets-browser`).**
- 1a: wall-clock time. The engine reads the Teensy RTC; a time is valid only from 2025 to 2099 (`wallclock::valid`) and
  otherwise shows `TIME NOT SET` — never the build time (legacy `RtcTime` seeded an invalid clock from `__DATE__`).
  Measured: the Teensy loader sets the RTC to the computer's **local** time at each upload (one hour ahead of UTC in
  CET), so the RTC is read as local time with a shown offset of 0 (EEPROM bytes 0–3). `!ENGINE time [unix]`,
  `!ENGINE tz [minutes]`, `scripts/engine_set_time.py`; `#ENGINE,time,...` at boot. Native
  `test_content_engine_wall_clock` (mutations 3 / 4; the pre-1970 branch unreachable by valid times).
- 1b: the store's completed writes are stamped with the wall time (`last_save=…,saved=22:17` in `!ENGINE time`), for
  the browser's `SAVED 14:32`. Seen on the device after a loop resize. Image `3c20915b…`, boot verified.

**2026-11-08 — Fixed-memory engine: LOOP_EDIT one undo step a visit; F2 on 25 notches.**
- Owner: "the number of undos explode on the loop length edits". A LOOP_EDIT visit is now one undo step: a length or
  start change replaces the state the visit's previous change made while that is still the slot's current (its
  identity checked, so an undo inside the visit makes the next change a step again); leaving LOOP_EDIT or switching
  track ends the visit (`SlotTransport::adopt`, `History::replaceState`). Replaced rotations' copies are released.
- Owner: F2 over 128 steps was niggly and the motor holds 25 notches, sending the notch number. F2 is now 25 positions:
  1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 bar, 1–16 bars, 32, 64, 96, 128 bars (CC 101 = the notch, its motor parked on the notch
  below an off-scale length); LENGTH shows fractions under a bar ("1/16", "3/4").
- Fix (owner: notched, F2 showed only 1/16 and 128): the DROID's notched output is the notch number, which its CC out
  saturates at 127 past notch 0. CC 101 is read over 0–127 again, to the nearest of the 25 notches
  (`Surface::notchOfCc`), and the motor parked at a notch's value (`ccOfNotch`): continuous works as is; notched needs
  the patch to scale the notch back to 0–1 (output ÷ 24, start value × 24). Image `3719a15b…`, boot verified; owner
  confirmed on the DROID ("yes that worked").

  / `oled-phase <v>` set the SSD1322's front clock (0xB3, boot 0x91) / phase lengths (0xB1, boot 0xE2) live, and
  `frame-ms <n>` the frame period (33); no argument reports. Not kept over a reboot. Goal: a panel scan as fast as the

  the clock cannot remove it; the boot value stays.

  written to the 64 GRAM rows not shown and the display start line (0xA1) moved to them once complete. Tear-free only
  if the controller applies the start line at its next frame (not in the datasheet). Legacy (`teensy41-capture-serial`)
  still builds; it never turns it on. Image `b20f4a6f…`, boot verified.

**2026-11-06 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.8h saves never wait for the card.**
- The last save hold (up to 8 ms) was SdFat stopping a write stream and waiting while the card programmed it. The
  engine now writes the store as its own stream, stops it without waiting and moves on while the card is busy; a
  save counts as done only once the card is idle again. On the device the worst save step is now under 1 ms (was up
  to 9.8 ms; ~30 ms before E9.8g) and every slot reloads after a reboot.

**2026-11-06 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.8g saves write sectors only (the A / B store).**
- Slots and the selection are saved into one preallocated file, `/MidiLooper/engine/store.bin`, written sector by
  sector with no file-system work: two copies a slot, a save writes the other one and seals it last, so an interrupted
  save keeps the current copy (DEC-253). The owner's card moved to 32 GB (the store is 277 MB). On the device the 22
  slots moved into the store and reload from it; the worst save grain fell from ~30 ms to 2.5–9.8 ms, which is now
  this card's own sector-write time (open: a non-blocking write).

**2026-11-06 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.8f external-clock stalls fixed.**

  the clock timeout restarted output. While following an external clock the engine now sends an Active Sensing byte
  after 20 ms of USB silence: no gap in a 4-minute run, owner "rock stable". Saves write one sector a grain; a save
  still holds the loop ~30 ms on file open / close / rename (open).

  the earlier decision — the owner is asked about importing them (E9.7c). The engine now also plays each track on its
  MIDI channel, as the old firmware does.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.7a saving and loading (owner decisions).**
- Nothing is written to the card until saving is approved once on the device (the new engine folder remembers it);
  then a changed slot autosaves 2 s after its last change, never mid-take or mid-edit, via a temp file and rename; boot
  loads every engine file, naming any that fail. PSRAM budget restated to 6,812,948 B (NOTE_EDIT selection and
  persistence state lines). V1 import (LSV1) is E9.7b.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.6 piano roll from tiles.**
- Tiles now follow every slot's state (commits, Undo / Redo, edits; Clear blanks), the shown slot gets span tiles, a
  take on it is painted live until its tiles show it, and `PianoRollRender` draws the note layer in bands from tiles at
  the legacy geometry. On the Teensy a whole frame takes 233 µs.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.5 NOTE_EDIT for the surface.**
- `NoteEditSession` gathers the selection as the piano roll shows it, with each note's recorded geometry (overlaps stay
  derived, so the edited note drives and the others adapt), runs edits as E: steps heard from the next boundary, and
  returns each step's focus token on undo / redo; leave keeps one undo step, abandon restores.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.4 gestures, input and bounded late join (owner decisions).**
- `TrackControl` keeps the legacy gesture timing: queued Record on the bar or the playing slot's loop start (waiting for
  the one writer), queued Stop on the bar, slot switches on the grid or at the loop end (window 0 composed ahead, so
  the new slot's downbeat lands on the commit tick), undoable Clear, mute / solo, transport stop / start, live thru.
- Owner: one sounding slot per track for now (layering and jam later); bounded late join for every transition —
  within min(24 ticks, 25 ms), notes still sounding start late with their end, missed short notes are skipped, the
  Clock only adopts what workers prepared.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.3 Clock path to the MIDI ports.**
- Each Clock tick now plays every track into the output hub and out of its three ports (DIN, USB device, USB host),
  with per-track routing, no stuck notes on a routing change or Undo, and re-strikes kept apart. On the Teensy a tick
  for two tracks costs at most 11 µs. The firmware's `ClockManager` and MIDI senders switch over at E9.8.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.2 engine root, placed and measured on the Teensy (owner: two sweep windows).**
- The whole engine now lives in two placed regions with one `init()` (1.9 ms on the Teensy over unzeroed memory), a
  memory census and budget checks, and a main-loop job service: two tracks record, overdub and play exactly under the
  scheduler on the device (longest grain 342 µs, no missed deadline, checkpoint sets swept). PSRAM budget restated to
  6,796,508 B (two sweep scratch windows); RAM2 143,360 B. Two defects found and fixed: poisoned cold-start leases at
  init, and the Record prepare replaying a 2^30-tick provisional loop.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.1b handoff without a gap.**
- After Record Stop the take plays whole from its first tick, and after an overdub wrap the cycle's new notes play
  from window 0 of the next cycle: window 0 is composed ahead (from the recording so far) and handed over at the
  boundary. A freed-buffer defect in the first version of the handoff was found by the tests and fixed.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E9.1 slot transport (owner: publish at the wrap).**
- Record / overdub / Stop / Undo / Redo now drive the writer, manifests, history and playback tracks end to end on a
  Clock timeline; one writer at a time (`Busy`). A wrap with a note held across the loop end publishes at once and is
  completed in place when the note is released. Known gap for E9.1b: after Record Stop the first window is silent,
  and after a wrap the cycle's new notes are heard from window 1.

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E8.2a V1 import, exact current content only (owner decision).**

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E8.1 engine slot file (owner: new format, new folder).**

**2026-11-05 — Fixed-memory engine: E6.2f live occupancy while recording.**

**2026-11-04 — DEC-251: tile preparation can no longer abort the device.**

**2026-11-04 — DEC-136.4b closeout: content-provenance verdict and R3 reachability (no production change).**
- **Content parity.** The first divergent representation is the routed manifest's currency: after a slot clear and a
  new take, `ImportSourceKey` is identical (`loop=0, prev=1, cpr=1, inventory` equal), so the reader serves the cleared
  take's manifest and never imports the new one. Raw capture, frozen source, committed passes and display are correct.
  On the device every run's committed playback is the previous run's take (also on the pre-slice A/B image). Host RED
  gated `CONTENT_PARITY_RED`; the snapshot path (default image) is unaffected (default-gate guard).
- **R3.** Reachable on the host: with root work over about one frozen bar, 23-24 yields, no takeover in 8 traversals,
  job bound and frozen source held for the whole run. Device workloads without overdub finish in ~300 ticks; under
  Overdub-load lane cadence it is unproven. Proposal: yield at the frozen bar's latest safe start (priced), not at the
  handoff; a convergence guarantee needs root progress to survive a yield (separate ruling).
- DEC-136 item 4 entry added to the decision log. Native full 4,009 / 0 failed.
- [Evidence](../../openspec/changes/revision-manifest-prototype/evidence/2026-11-03-audibility-and-publication-liveness.md)

  bars normally, the terminal bar alone, an off-grid default-partition start has none). The clock edge re-keys the
  frame (start, absolute deadline, partition) in O(1); the committed resolver accepts it.
- **Frozen priority (`b0d63d25`, `01e9e9eb`).** On the routed slot, with no retained view, the frozen reader's next bar
  outranks incomplete root work (only work that holds the builder yields); frozen builds are never superseded while
  still owed; an authorized frozen frame that served out expires instead of being labelled `ServingViewSourceStale`.
- **Host.** Lane gate 33/33; native full 4,008 / 0 failed; ITCM byte-identical on both images (304 B and 64 B headroom).
- **Device** (succprobe `1149748f…`, `session_20261104_104642`): no post-stop silence (A/B `972e955a`: 62-97 s silent);
  takeover at 10752; job released after the takeover. (The root-window MIDI equalled its committed successors, but
  both came from the stale manifest of the previous take; corrected in the closeout.)
- **Open (owner):** R3 root liveness under cost; a ~200-tick frozen-versus-committed content offset (four notes repeat
  at the takeover; also on the A/B image); C5.3b production successors; the default image is not device-qualified here.

**2026-11-03 — Wrap Clock breakdown: the wrap snapshot journal is 96% of the wrap; the C3.4 deadline answered nothing (wrap probe).**
- **Measured** (`1731cac3`, two sweeps: `captures/session_20261103_190327.log`, `captures/session_20261103_190834.log`):
  - The wrap took 1.33 s and 1.40 s, with 99.99% of it accounted for by the probe's steps.
  - `queueOverdubWrapSnapshotJournal` took 1.28 s and 1.35 s, about 3 ms per sealed Add (428 and 436 Adds).
  - Sealing took 3 ms. The C3.4 deadline answered 0 owed completions: the worker had discharged them all before the
    wrap.
- **Cause by code reading.** For every row, `appendPairedNoteEventChanges` calls `parent.findNote`. For an Add, the
  note is not in the parent, so `LoopSnapshot::findNote` falls back to scanning every pitch. The wrap therefore costs
  O(sealed Adds × parent notes).
- **Boot fix.** `6ec640bb` (construct-only boot init) reverts 49eccad3's destroy-first, which was in the default image
  until then. `72d9e280` (default image) boots.
- **Open.**
  - Probe image `9400e352` (exactly this tree) never enumerates on USB and leaves no CrashReport. The failure follows
    the flash code layout: adding temporary breadcrumb code (`1731cac3`) makes it boot. This is a latent defect with
    an unknown owner.
  - Waiting on an owner ruling: the wrap-ownership RED now targets the journal, not the deadline.
- [Evidence](../../openspec/changes/revision-manifest-prototype/evidence/2026-11-03-c5-3b-successor-grant-budget.md)

**2026-11-03 — DEC-247: a full deferred overdub completion set keeps the completion owed, and the NoteOff derives nothing (`c0e8cbd8`).**
- **Cause chain** (C5.3b overdub-phase traces):
  - The overdub MIDI cost was the full-set synchronous derive: 46-78 ms per NoteOff, 16-17.6 s per sweep.
  - The set filled after a source-generation move. That move is the DEC-159 / C3.5 Record publication supersession,
    which the owner kept as legitimate (the alternative of delaying session open was withdrawn), or the wrap commit.
  - The slow NoteOffs starved the worker, so the set stayed full.
- **Fix.**
  - On a full set, the note's `Add` row carries `consequenceOwed`. The worker promotes those rows into freed capacity,
    and the C3.4 seal deadline answers the rest with the retained path's rule.
  - Unchanged: capacity, generation invalidation, wrap semantics.
- **Host.** RED → GREEN (3 fixtures). The old synchronous answer also dropped a transform the retained path makes.
  Native full 3,968 / 0 failed.
- **Device** (`d4579ca9`, `captures/session_20261103_171618.log`):
  - Overdub Note messages: 17.95 s / max 78 ms → 0.81 s / 5.5 ms.
  - Worker discharges: 3 → 50.
- **Open (owner).** The wrap Clock grew from 3.0 to 4.30 s: the C3.4 wrap deadline answers the still-owed completions
  inside the Clock dispatch (`commitOverdubWrap`). Also open: the deferred stop route's swap does not materialize
  touched-coverage obligations (pre-existing).
- [Evidence](../../openspec/changes/revision-manifest-prototype/evidence/2026-11-03-c5-3b-successor-grant-budget.md)

**2026-11-02 — OLED dim/flicker with the overview strip: the STOPPED wrap-held completion re-walked the whole loop every frame (owner report); fixed.**
- **Cause.** Stage 3B in `resolveDisplayNotesByDrawSource` (from `8849c5e1`) called `Loop::appendOverdubPassDisplayNotes` on every STOPPED frame: every committed event of every active pass was read, edit-applied and reconstructed to find the few loop-crossing rows. On track 8 slot 3 (25,344 ticks, 256 notes; `session_20261102_164414`) resolve went from ~0.5 ms while playing to ~40 ms per frame once STOPPED, so the OLED ran at ~9 fps (pulse of the selected track label slowed, flicker).
- **Fix.** `DisplayManager::stoppedWrapHeldCompletion` memoises the wrap-held set per loop content (`loopId`, `playbackRevision`, `canonicalStorageGeneration`, length; dropped by `invalidateLiveDisplayCache`); the frame merges it with `DisplayWindowUtils::mergeWrapHeldDisplayNotes`, the same rule the append uses (now shared).
- **Host.** `test_stopped_draw_source_snapshot_append_wrap_held_183741` extended: merged memo == direct append, two frames. FULL 3,941 cases, 8 skipped, 3,933 passed.
- **Follow-up (owner: "not dim any more, but the window isn't rendered").** A framebuffer dump showed the overview strip drawn at gray 0-3, which the panel shows as near-black. Notes are now 3/6 (outside/inside window) and the window box 5/8. Capture builds keep `!FB_DUMP` (`DisplayManager::emitFrameBufferDump`, rendered by `scripts/render_display_dump.py`; see `MANUAL_TEST_CAPTURE_SESSION.md`). Image `9c1ca13cbf388dee`, boot `crash=0`. Track 6's number has the same framebuffer level (4) as the other unselected numbers, so a dimmer look there is panel-side; the owner confirmed the panel looks right on this image.
- **Device** (`31d473953c26db29`, boot `crash=0`, `BOOT,load,ok`, same slot STOPPED after boot): resolve ~0.62 ms, frame ~28 ms, ~16 DMA frames/s (was ~70 ms / ~9.3/s). The stopped-after-transport-stop path was not re-run.

**2026-11-02 — a price-refused routed demand is discharged into a quiescent `PriceRefusal` (5.1, DEC-246 amendment 27, owner ruling B); the device gate is still owed.**
- **A (first-window price input).** Already interval-based: the position bound is `densestWindowRows(identity, loop,
  1536)`, the densest bar-aligned 1,536-tick span from manifest metadata. Admission prices the counted requested
  interval. 25,344 is the loop extent only. This is now asserted (`priceRefusal.coverage.lengthTicks == 2 bars <
  loop`).
- **B.** `main.cpp`'s per-turn committed demand asks for the playhead's own window (lead about zero). DEC-147 refused
  it, and the refusal left it pending forever (`win_busy`). On the routed slot the refused demand is now discharged and
  a `PriceRefusal` {source, epoch, interval, price, available lead} stays in its place. The per-turn requester does not
  re-issue a demand whose interval starts inside the refused one: one refusal per span, not per turn.
- **Scope.** Other slots keep DEC-108 §13(c)'s retained-refusal promise; three fixtures in
  `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` pin it. Making the invariant general needs an owner ruling on DEC-108.
- **Host.** RED `test_5_1_a_price_refused_demand_leaves_no_pending_owner` (the lane drives main's per-turn demand):
  GREEN, and the mutation fails it. FULL 3,941 cases, 8 skipped, 3,933 passed. Per-slot runtime +64 B on the reader
  image and +56 B on the default image (extmem); RAM1 unchanged.
- **Device.** Image `db23c569a8d88e80` flashed. The first gate attempt was refused at attach (transport running), and
  the second stalled in the harness before its scenario started, so there is no outcome yet.

**2026-11-02 — orphaned ready successor reclaimed (5.1, DEC-246 amendment 27); track 8 is now blocked by the DEC-147 lead price, not by roles.**
- **The leak** (device `session_20261102_155425`). The Record presentation retired while its owed successor was still
  being built. The build was published as `ready` at 88.0 s, but its adopter was gone, so no frame owned it. Beside the
  retained view it held the role every build publishes into (`role_ready_occupied`), giving `win_busy rl=0` across the
  stop and the restart.
- **Fix.** On an Idle frame, `serviceRollingPlaybackWindow` retires a complete, unpublished `ready` that nothing else
  can adopt: no demand, no build, no Record-return job, no launch, no pending promise. It goes through
  `retireSupersededReady`, or straight to the build role when the slot has none. The new row is
  `win_orphan_successor_reclaimed`.
- **Host.** RED `test_5_1_an_orphaned_ready_successor_returns_its_build_role` (injected state; failed before the fix,
  GREEN now). FULL 3,940 cases, 8 skipped, 3,932 passed.
- **Device** (succprobe `e19471b492a9c901`, boot `crash=0` and `BOOT,load,ok`, `captures/session_20261102_161218.log`):
  - The role stays free throughout (`rl=1`).
  - Track 8's committed demand was refused as `handoff_unreachable` at 88.07 s and stays pending (`dm=1`, no build),
    so the requester sits at `win_busy` before and after the restart. No first manifest window serves.
  - This is the lead price for a dense 25,344-tick window: the pending C5.3b measured-price decision.

**2026-11-02 — Record presentation deadlock on the manifest route fixed (5.1, DEC-246 amendment 27); a restart build-role leak remains.**
- **The deadlock.** On the routed slot, the Record job and its presentation waited for the root snapshot's session exit
  and then for a served window carrying the manifest identity. Their own hold kept that window from building, so a
  dense take stopped into play never reached manifest serving (host: `win_blocked_by_budget` after two refused spans,
  because the non-cold request paid the DEC-147 lead price).
- **Fix.** `Track::manifestTakesOverRecordReturn`: a manifest servable for the loop's current revision is the routed
  slot's takeover, in the presentation loop's gate, its snapshot-exit hold, and the retirement step's snapshot-exit
  and served-window holds. The frozen-Capture-still-serving hold and the frozen-window release are unchanged; unrouted
  slots are unchanged.
- **Host.** New RED `test_5_1_routed_dense_take_presentation_yields_to_the_manifest_lane` (GREEN; the mutation with the
  helper forced false fails). FULL 3,939 cases, 8 skipped, 3,931 passed. RAM1 unchanged (padding 936).
- **Device** (succprobe `4931646dca91c158`, `captures/session_20261102_155425.log`, sweep with `--lane-cadence-deny none`):
  - During play after the take, `rw` dropped to 0 and the manifest build took ownership (`ow=1,bld=1`), so the
    deadlock is cleared.
  - After the stop and restart, track 8 sat at `win_busy` with `dm=0,bld=0,ow=0,rl=0` for 90 s, so there was no first
    manifest window. The stop tore down the in-flight build without returning its build role. That is a separate
    defect and is next.
  - Tracks 1–7 were lane-served after the restart in this run.

**2026-11-02 — test tooling: tiered native runner (`scripts/test_native.py`); sharded FULL in 80 s warm / 163 s cold (was 741 s).**

**2026-10-29 — the boot hold now ends at the playback set, and the boot drain keeps that set ordered first (DEC-196; flashed and device-verified, `bea5a99b…`).** Owner report corrected the record: *"if I start playing directly after boot only track 5 plays"*. `captures/session_20261029_113133.log` showed the earlier "all tracks by 18.5 s" read was wrong — **18.47 s is the owner's transport stop**, and every commit after it happened because the transport was stopped. Because the drain flag also keeps `canRunBackgroundLoadLoopNow()` true, a Play pressed during the hold no longer blocks the set. **2026-10-29 — root-bearing loop persistence landed natively: a normal record/overdub stop now persists the slot body with its root, and a body that could not get one is re-written once its root settles (DEC-195; native + build green, NOT flashed).** Owner report: every boot restored rootless bodies, so playback had no root and a take had to be recorded first. Cause is admission order, not the writer: the stop admits the save from the commit, so at the loop write's `Header` stage the selected root is always one revision behind, and `decideLoopPersistBodyFormat` only waited when it was already coverage-current — the settle branch was dead on the only path that needed it (device: `PERS,result` 19.195 s, `snapshot_unit,kind=publish` 19.619 s). **Landed:** the wait now covers a publication owed for the current committed state, bounded by `kLoopPersistSettleWaitMs` (1500 ms) and `kLoopPersistSettleMaxDeferrals` (2048), closing the slot temp file while it waits and never waiting inside a synchronous drain; a body finalized without a root for a slot holding committed passes records `currentSetLoopSlotRootRewritePending[track][slot]`, and `StorageManager::serviceRootlessSlotRepersist` (one call per idle turn beside the persistence turn) re-admits exactly that slot through the existing dirty/admit/request path once `hasSettledPublishedSnapshotForSave()` holds, clearing the record before the admission. DEC-180's equivalence admission, the loader, and the playback path are unchanged. Also: the LSV1 save scratch selected the external pool whenever `ARDUINO` was defined, so native suites that define it could never write an LSV1 body; the guard now also requires `__IMXRT1062__` (device unchanged). Gates: `test_storage_loop_io` 67/67, `test_storage_drain_restore` 24/24, full native **3597 cases / 3 failed (the pre-existing DEC-193/DEC-194 REDs) / 7 skipped / 3586 succeeded**, `teensy41-capture-serial` SUCCESS at RAM1 `variables 96,192` / ITCM `code 391,992 + padding 1,224` (floor 840). Device acceptance is open: record, stop, power cycle, then the restored slot must report a non-zero `root_rev` and play without a new take. **2026-10-27 — 4.19 display source retention implemented; the enforced immediate-wrap display regression is GREEN (firmware + fixtures; nothing on device).**
The measured root cause stands: a wrap appends a pass and advances `playbackRevision`, so the completed display source stopped being qualified, the provider fell through, and the next `begin()`→`reset()` destroyed the last correct generation. The settled contract ([handoff](../../docs/Plans/display_source_retention_handoff.md)) is now implemented in the **existing** `BoundedDisplaySession` owner with **zero new `Loop` state** (the 1,848 B `sizeof(Loop)` pin is untouched), no new scheduler and no ownership transfer: the candidate records its pass-set prefix identity as the Order phase enumerates it, promotion at the existing publish edge `std::move`s the finished rows into a retained envelope priced `16·capacity` (named `retained_capacity` over-cap refusal, previous envelope kept), and `resetCandidate()` is split from `reset()` so a re-key or pass-set change keeps the envelope. Retention identity is an **exact predicate read at reuse time** — request identity including `canonicalStorageGeneration`, the whole edit-row identity, then a walk of the **retained prefix only** — so a wrap's appended pass keeps serving while any state change inside the prefix refuses (undo→redo requalifies, proven by equality against an independent rebuild). **2026-10-26 — MIDI Start resumes a track that owes an offline deferred stop job (regression fixed, native + build verified, not yet on device).**
User session_20261026_223337: after Record plus several overdubs a MIDI Stop left the track STOPPED (`DISP,3,STOPPED`), and every later MIDI Start (115.971/118.664/120.871/124.400) logged `Transport started` but resumed nothing — only the track-level record/stop gesture (143.906, then 151.115) returned PLAYING. Cause: `d120e0c2` replaced `isOverdubStopping()` with `hasPendingDeferredOverdubStop()` inside `TrackManager::hasActiveOrPendingCapture()`, and `ClockManager::onMidiStart()`/`toggleTransport()` skip their whole resume fan-out while that predicate is true — so the offline finalization window after the stop edge blocked every resume for as long as the job stayed pending. Repair: new narrow predicate `hasLiveCaptureBlockingTransportStart()` (recording / armed / overdubbing / inline stop winding down / queued record — a track in TRACK_STOPPED that only owes a deferred stop job is not a live capture; its role closed at its own stop edge) used at the three transport-start call sites; `hasActiveOrPendingCapture()` keeps its stronger meaning for the SESSION_CAPTURE motion guard and any future capture-safety read. RED→GREEN fixture `transportStartResumesTrackWithPendingDeferredOverdubStop` in test_midi_input_clock_integration (real Track/TrackManager/ClockManager; fails as "MIDI Start must resume a STOPPED track…" with the old gate). Full native 3,479 cases / 7 skipped / 0 failed; teensy41-capture-serial BUILD, RAM1 unchanged (variables 96,192; padding 3,224 ≥ floor 840), no HEX claim, not uploaded, not committed. The parked deferred stop that stretched the window ("companion path stalled; raw pass only" at 133.000) remains task4.11/4.4 work under immediate-record-overdub-handoff; device acceptance of this fix is open.

No admission constant was touched; no owner moved (task scope, not an ownership transfer, so no DEC). **2026-10-20 — I5 — 3.14c — the undo edge asks the publication owner, and the owner rebuilds from the pass inventory (firmware + tests; **DEC-150**; task 3.14 stays open).** The owed "request currency through the existing publication owner" is in place and it needed a **shape**, not just a call. The edge asks once the entry is fully applied (`applyPublishedSnapshotSelect`; inside the refreshes it stamped a coverage the caller then invalidated, so it could never publish current) and skips only a root that already covers the live revision; stale is still refused by name (`SourceNotCurrent`), so DEC-073 is intact. A publication already in flight is **replaced**, not left alone: its enumeration is older, so the last edge before the idle lane runs publishes at its own coverage (the coalescing guard this slice first shipped published the older candidate and left the slot refused — red-proved; an independent review found it would also have suppressed the request the record/overdub undo always made). An edit-pass undo leaves the committed passes unchanged, so the incremental republish's diff is empty and the owner correctly found nothing to freeze (measured: published coverage stayed **1** while `playbackRevision` reached **4**, box cleared with no candidate); a companion change can only add or update, so a withdrawn overlay could not be retracted either. `Loop::requestCommittedPassesRebuild` is the second shape: same lane, same coverage stamping, candidate enumerated against an **empty** parent, so it is the active pass inventory plus the active overlays. Edit-pass entries use it (including committed-pass entries that also carried companion batches); entries that only changed committed passes keep the incremental form. A stop's session-exit queue that adopts a rebuild box re-enumerates the identities it does not track (`adoptNewInventoryRowsInto`) before stamping, so an empty-parent candidate never claims a pass it omits; the shared enumeration stays **literal** — duplicate ids are inventory rows, pinned by `test_note_edit_entry_boundary` (the first form of that fix collapsed them and was replaced). Verified in the 3.14 fixture through the real `undoForLoop` edge on an owner-built root: the served window is 4 committed + 3 overlay note pairs before the undo, refused by name while the request is pending, and exactly the post-undo effective content afterwards (6 events, still-active batch included) — the retraction is measured against `copyEffectiveCommittedEventsInRange`, not assumed. Red-proofs: no request / pending publication left in place / rebuild downgraded to incremental, each failing at its own named assertion. Host **221/221** (baseline confirmed at 221), `test_note_edit_entry_boundary` **104/104**, full native **3338 / 7 skipped / 3331 succeeded**, target build SUCCESS with RAM1 unchanged (`variables 96,192`, `code 392,216`, `padding 1,000`). Named limits: a change with **no** requesting edge can still publish an intermediate root (refused by name; the next edge asks again), `adoptNewInventoryRowsInto` has no fixture (it needs a live stop right after an undo), and a rebuild costs one full pass enumeration on the idle lane. Still open: 3.7d's device read, 4.5.

**2026-10-20 — I5 — 3.14c — the publication-owner request is possible, but a republish cannot represent a note-edit undo (read-only; nothing shipped, G0 BLOCKED on a design fork).** The owed call was implemented and measured, then withdrawn. The *edge* can ask: a cold helper calling `Loop::requestCommittedPassesRepublish` at the **end** of `applyPublishedSnapshotSelect` (inside the refreshes it stamped a coverage the caller then invalidated) leaves a pending republish, one queued pass, `pendingSnapshotFromLoadedPasses()==false`, and still answers `SourceNotCurrent` — DEC-073 intact. The *owner* then finds nothing to publish: the record pass is already in the parent, so its diff is empty; the batch the undo disabled is no longer active, so the companion branch skips it; the empty-candidate path clears the box. Measured: after 20 000 owner turns the published coverage stayed **1** while `playbackRevision` reached **4**, with no new root. Deeper: `appendEditRowChange` only adds/updates, so a companion that becomes `Disabled` has **no removal representation** — re-stamping a no-op diff current would be silent-wrong and was rejected. 3.14c therefore needs a shape decision: (A) **rebuild-from-empty** for the request (recommended; record/overdub path untouched), (B) companion removals in the snapshot change set, or (C) a coverage repair that overturns DEC-073's contract. **Resolved the same day:** option **A** landed as DEC-150 (see the newest entry above). **2026-10-20 — I5 — 4.5 — the moving closure now exists on the **demoted** serving handoff: an edit that keeps a sounding note and moves its end behind the playhead closes it once, at the edit, instead of a whole loop later (firmware + native; **DEC-148**; 4.5 stays open for 3.14c, displayed provenance and the device leg).** I9 closed this for the **merged** route and recorded the demoted one as still owed, with its reason: the merged store there is a two-bar slice, `reconcilePlaybackLedgerAfterFullLoopRebuild` returns early on a slice by design, and the lane's seam deliberately closes nothing from a window (absence is not removal — the 6.5 A/B fixture measures exactly that). The fix is the **phase half of the handoff's own predicate** applied to a stream that is not whole-loop authority (`ActiveNoteLedger::planExpiredClosures`): only a NoteOff the stream *carries* at or behind the served position is evidence, the served position is `playbackClosureServeFloor` with the lane projection phase as the fallback (`Track::playbackClosureFloorForSlot`, `UINT32_MAX` = nothing served ⇒ nothing closed), and the closure is emitted at the edit's own edge through the same wire-and-ledger order as the handoff, before the presence settlement. A closure the ledger no longer holds is now **suppressed** rather than re-emitted (`applyClosureSettlementForSlot`), which is the spec's own obsolete-closure rule. **RED first** on the real demoted harness (interval window adopted, two obligations articulated, edit landing after the moved end's tick): the settlement named zero closures. Detail: [`EXECUTION-DEVICE.md`](openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-repositioning/EXECUTION-DEVICE.md) and [`DESIGN.md`](openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-repositioning/DESIGN.md) §10.

**2026-10-19 — I5 — 4.5/6.4 — a handoff-lead refusal is now a *position* refusal: the owner re-requests the demand at the next span (**DEC-147**; firmware, native RED→GREEN, three device attempts; 4.5 and 6.4 stay open).** The `:5393` guard carried two terms under one name. They are now separate: only `canCompleteWithinLead` (this demand's own derived build cost against the lead it was positioned against) is a position term; `playbackViewAdmissionKeepsAdmittedDeadlines` stays **terminal**, so admitted-deadline protection is unchanged. On a lead-only refusal of the lane's own `Requested` demand the refusal records the spent handoff on the frame, sets it `Idle`, retires the source and **releases the retained record** (DEC-108 §13(a) would otherwise coalesce the refused deadline onto the next request and re-impose the position), and emits `win_repositioned`; the **creation path** then pushes its boundary to the first span at or after the refused handoff, so the retry is a fresh qualification of a new interval through the path the device already exercises. Strict advance plus a whole-traversal `win_blocked_by_request` bounds the episode. **Why the creation path:** a lane-side re-request was measured to leave `pendingViewRequest_.active == 0` and `coveragePreparation == Idle` (frame waits forever); in-place repositioning at `AwaitAdmission` is unsound because the counted source belongs to the old interval. **Native:** two new fixtures (reposition→serve with ordered receipts, stale→not repositioned); 3.10's dense-shape fixture changes verdict **by design** — the dense interval is still refused by name and never adopted, but the demand moves to a span it can afford and that span is served. Focused **217/217**, full native **3,334 cases / 7 skipped / 3,327 succeeded / 0 failed**; lane image `code 392,376 + padding 840` (floor, no re-base). **Device: the demand shape was NOT reproduced in three runs** — 24-bar (transport start finds `rw=1` record-return: `win_blocked` with `sv=1,rt=1,rl=0`), 32-bar no-boot (no boot sweep, `win_track_not_playing` 72), 32-bar boot (boot sweep captured, but `t=7,s=3` reads `win_not_servable, sv=0, rt=0` — the restored root is not current yet). The refusal control opens its demand at `pl=1, rw=0, rt=1, rl=1`, so the next device step is a settle-and-replay leg that starts transport **after** the restore completes and the record-return window retires. No `win_serving`/`win_ready` claim is made. Detail: [`2026-10-19-s45-repositioning/DESIGN.md`](../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-repositioning/DESIGN.md) §9–§10 and [`EXECUTION-DEVICE.md`](../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-repositioning/EXECUTION-DEVICE.md).

**2026-10-19 — I5 — 4.5 — production containment is wired: the owner-level *"no serving route at all"* predicate (**DEC-146**; firmware, native evidence; 4.5 stays open).** The recorded blocker was a **missing owner** — the first wiring (withdrawn 2026-10-06, F1) judged at the serving resolver's *rejections*, which are exactly the turns the retained merged fallback serves, so it closed a sounding another route was about to play. The predicate now asks the **cross-route** question **after** route selection: `bridge || bound view || prepared pair || paged emission` — if any is selected, containment is not asked at all; otherwise the **cold** owner `Track::containPlaybackTurnIfNoRouteForSlot` decides whether the merged catch-all's **own bounded window** covers this phase (a short loop's store is whole-loop and always covers; a demoted loop serves a window, and a window whose build was refused this turn covers nothing), and only a non-covering phase reaches `applyLastResortForSlot`. Two properties are part of the rule: **availability, not content** (an event-empty route is still a route, so a sustained note is never silenced for an empty window) and **coverage, not freshness** (a stale window that covers still serves — the last coherent revision). `applyLastResortForSlot` still asks `containmentForSlot`, so a slot whose **published** coverage remains answers `ServeLastCoherentRevision` and is left alone; the application stays slot-scoped (`silenceSlotMidiOutput` + ledger clear), rebuilds nothing, never touches the transport. **DEC-145's latch gate is deliberately NOT lifted** — this slice adds no clear boundary, so containment can *act* only in the lane image, where a fault can exist. **Measured:** RED→GREEN fixture `test_the_last_resort_is_applied_only_when_no_serving_route_covers_the_phase` (demoted 64-bar slot, fault latched through its own owner, no published window, merged build refused → the real MIDI turn applies the last resort **once**; control with the build allowed silences nothing), RED exactly one failure with the production change reverted; focused **215/215**, full native **3332 / 3 325 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, capture build **SUCCESS** with **+128 B of ITCM** (`code 392,216 + padding 1,000`; 160 B above the 840 floor; **no re-base** — the first inline form was +192 B, so the projection arithmetic moved into the cold owner, below the withdrawn form's +144 B). No upload. **Correction (same day, after measuring it):** the lane-enabled qualification image is **not** over budget — it builds at `code 392,376 + padding 840`, exactly the approved floor (and byte-identical with and without this slice, so the lane image pays nothing) — so the device leg is not blocked by the image; the lane image simply has zero headroom left. **6.4 input, measured:** `DIAG,win_gate` is state-change-emitted, and across **every** log name in `captures/` (20 446 rows) `win_serving` and `win_ready` have **0** occurrences, while `win_requested` / `win_waiting` / `win_blocked_by_request` form a matched **25 / 25 / 25** set: every demand episode ever recorded was created, waited, and blocked — **the lane's own frame has never advanced past `Waiting` on device**, so the windows F-7/F-8 saw served came from a different producer (the serving gather; those rows read `al=0`, i.e. the demand lane excluded the loop). Observing `win_ready → win_serving` therefore needs a demand that *completes*, not a longer run — and the 32-bar run (`captures/i5-s64-f8-parity-32bar-01`) already **is** that configuration (`av=1, al=1`): it requested (`rq=12`), waited while building (`bld=1`), then blocked by request with the build gone and **no free role** (`rl=0`), so the completed successor is never adopted and the deciding term is **already on the wire**: the same instant emits `build_drop,handoff_unreachable` (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp:5399`), i.e. `request.reason = CannotCompleteBeforeHandoff` — the lane refuses a window it cannot finish before the handoff it is positioned for, and `win_blocked_by_request` is its reading of that reason. So 6.4 needs **no new field**; it needs a *successful* episode. The variable is density/contention, not length or alignment (both satisfied): native serves grains instantly and reaches `Ready` → `Serving`, while on device the 24-bar window competes with already-admitted deadlines. A new native oracle pins the successful order (`win_requested → win_ready → win_serving`; focused **215/215**, full native **3332 / 3 325 / 7 / 0**). A requested low-contention preset variant was **not** run and cannot help: the refusal is measured at **38.7 ms** after admission (requested 2 369 387 376 µs → `handoff_unreachable` 2 369 426 081 µs), and the only predicates that drop there (`canCompleteWithinLead(handoffLeadTicks(...))`, `playbackViewAdmissionKeepsAdmittedDeadlines`) are functions of the request's **phase against its handoff**, not of load. The phase is set by the firmware's switch schedule (`MidiButtonActions.cpp:56`, quantised whenever the clock runs), far below host gesture granularity. The two variants that could have removed the sibling (silence the source, or drop quantisation to take the launch path) either cannot disable the outgoing slot before the boundary or would record over the registered target. So 6.4's device `win_serving` needs a firmware positioning/retry change; the 24/32-bar captures stay the refusal control. A native oracle now pins the successful order (`win_requested → win_ready → win_serving`), full native **3332 / 3 325 / 7 / 0**. **Still owed in 4.5:** displayed provenance (RWO **S4e**), the device leg, 3.7b's legacy-emission removal (untouched — the predicate counts those branches), and the moving closure inside a long/demoted slot's serving handoff (3.7a/3.14). Detail: [`2026-10-19-s45-no-serving-route/EXECUTION.md`](../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-no-serving-route/EXECUTION.md).

**2026-10-19 — I5 — 4.5 — the deadline-contract fault is latched only where a boundary can clear it (firmware, one `#if`; native evidence; 4.5 stays open).** **G0 first:** containment's blocker is a **missing owner** — `containmentForSlot` asks a *coverage* question about the published window, while a refused window route is still served that turn from a live pair, paged emission, a record-return window or the merged fallback (`TrackPlaybackHotPath.cpp:337–343`), so *no coverage* is not *no serving route*; and a second defect — the latch is **set on a path the default image runs** (`noteMissedTraversalForSlot` ← `serviceAdmittedDeadlineMisses`, called unconditionally) while **both** clear sites are the lane's adoption boundary (`:1157` inside the flag, `:2210` reached only from `:4907`), which that image compiles out. Wiring a "real recovery" clear was **rejected as specified**: the promise route records the episode interval but **no revision**, so the lane's `servedIsCurrent` test has no meaning there. **DEC-145:** set the latch only under `PLAYBACK_WINDOW_ROLLING_ENABLED` — the same condition as its clears — so a fault exists only where a boundary can end it; the **breach report is unchanged in both images**, and nothing observable changes (neither `containmentForSlot` nor `deadlineContractFaultLatchedForSlot` has a production caller). **Measured:** RED→GREEN fixture `test_lag_breach_is_reported_but_not_latched_where_no_boundary_can_clear_it` (flag-on sibling keeps the latch and its clear); focused **322/322**, full native **3331 / 3324 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, capture build **SUCCESS** with RAM1 **byte-identical to HEAD** (`code 392,088 + padding 1,128`, no re-base). No upload, no device leg (no flashable image runs the lane). **Still owed in 4.5:** production containment / the approved last resort (the owner-level *"no serving route at all"* predicate, or 3.7b), displayed provenance (RWO **S4e**), the device leg (corrected the same day: the lane image **is** flashable at the 840-byte floor, so the leg is blocked by the receipt gap rather than by the image — see the 4.5e entry), and one recorded precondition — any image that wires containment must lift the latch gate with a clear site in that same image. [Latch gating](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-latch-gating/EXECUTION.md) · [G0](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-19-s45-containment-g0/INVESTIGATION.md).

**2026-10-19 — I5 — 4.3 — F-7 **PASS**: the demoted target's window-served stream equals `effective` in inventory and order across 79 advancing 1-bar window steps (device, no firmware change).** `content-review.json`: **`PASS`**, 3 cycles of 1 152 events, `inventory_equal` **and** `exact_order` true on all three, `cycle_cut: event_count`, `storage_matches_effective: true`. **Boundaries crossed:** 80 `playback_build` rows for the target, 1 536-tick (2-bar) span **stepping 768 ticks (1 bar)**, **24 distinct window starts** (`0…17 664`), **79 advances** — 25 positions per 25-bar cycle, so ≈25 boundaries per cycle; `extra=0` on every cycle means the one-bar overlap was served once. The device states the premises itself (`win_gate,t=7,s=3,len=19200,av=1,al=0` — demoted above the 16-bar bound, and not span-aligned, so the demand lane excludes it while the serving gather builds these windows). Residency holds after a cold boot (`record` = `effective` = 1 152 rows). Two host gaps closed: the pipeline reaches the target **without a record-toggle gesture** (`--select-track` via `slots.press_track`, `--dump-slot` → `!CAPTURE_CONTENT_SLOT n-1`, `--dump-only`), and the verifier cuts cycles on a **fully periodic** loop by event count (strict from the loop's first event, so a dropped event is reported rather than re-aligned away). New suites **4 OK + 4 OK**; defaults unchanged. **Open:** 4.3's closure obligation and overlap rule; F-8's length sweep; `oracle_complete` stays `False`; 6.4 open. **2026-10-19 — I5 — 4.4 — F-8's residency half is populated at five demoted lengths, and parity now stands at two (device, owner-authorized; the registered target was re-recorded three times; no firmware line, no upload).** The residency statement — `av=1` (above the 12 288-tick / 16-bar demotion bound) **and** `sv=1` (current view complete and published) on one `win_gate` row — is present across `captures/*/*.log` at **23, 24, 25, 26 and 32 bars** (17 664 / 18 432 / 19 200 / 19 968 / 24 576 ticks; 1 265 + 1 447 + 7 756 + 2 + 11 rows, overwhelmingly `pl=1`, from 2026-10-05 onward). Today's authorized runs re-recorded the registered target at 23 and 32 bars (the axis is exactly `record-bars`, 768 ticks/bar) with **758** and **1 028** `build_complete` rows at a 1 536-tick span, and the content pipeline gives `content-review.json` **`PASS`** at **24, 25 and 32 bars** — three demoted lengths, not one. The **24-bar** take first read `FAIL`, and the defect was the **oracle's**: its `effective` ends with the documented loop-boundary terminal Off (`tick = length - 1`, `NoteId = 0`), which playback does not serve, so the served loop is one event shorter than the dump and the event-count cut's fixed stride drifted one event per cycle (one missing **and** one extra row in *every* cycle). The verifier now drops only that documented residual and cuts at the served period — only when the strict cut does not already fit, so a dropped event still fails; `scripts.test_verify_playback_content_cycle_cut` **7 OK**. Re-running the 32-bar and F-7 captures reproduces `PASS` with `cycle_trimmed: null`. **Withdrawn:** an earlier entry today claimed this row had never been emitted and that it required a demoted + span-aligned + root-current + role-free slot; both were wrong (a `captures/*/serial.log`-only glob, and three qualifiers the rows refuse: `sv=1` occurs at `al=0`, at `rl=0`, and at `rt=0`). What survives: **`win_serving` and `win_ready` are absent from all 19 215 rows** — the demand lane's serving exit has never been recorded. **Open:** parity at further lengths, 3.6a's retained-source figure, 6.3's wider sweeps; `oracle_complete` stays `False`; 4.4 and 6.4 stay open. **2026-10-19 — I5 — 6.4 — the windowed leg's display oracle now pairs a phase by device time, and the drained capture decides (host tooling, no firmware change, no device run).** The slice the device leg named is landed, and the recorded captures are re-derived rather than re-run. `scripts/hitl/verify/display_window.py` brackets a phase's rows by **device time** (`_phase_rows`, reusing `windowed_lane.row_us`) with position kept only for markers that carry no stamp — applied to the freeze interval, both fallback samplings, the long-press snap comparison and the hold rows — because the Tier-A ring **retains** a row produced under transport and delivers it after the stop, so a position bracket reads the wrong phase in a drained capture. `verify_windowed_content_parity` re-derives `leg` from the **drained** capture it is handed and carries the runner's pre-drain report as `leg_run_report` provenance: the component that most needed the retained rows was the one read without them. **Measured on `captures/i5-s64-windowed-parity-01`/`-02`:** run 1's session log goes from `insufficient_disp_during_note_edit_freeze count=0` to `ok=True, issues=[], warnings=[]` (freeze row device `165833365`, `window_start 4876`, `window_bars 16`), so **run 1's combined verdict becomes `ok=True`, `issues=[]`** with lane and snapshot green — the case-1 artifact (`leg_exit_code: 2`) failed on the reading, not on the device. **2026-10-19 — I5 — DEC-144 — the matched terminal is realigned to continuous same-take serving across the generation handoff (native RED→GREEN + host + device `matched` PASS; three-group aggregate PASS; no firmware change).** The native production-path measurement settles the failed `matched` leg: a one-bar take stopped inside the bar has a DEC-136 pre-stop window prepared *before* its appends — `rows 0`, `captureToken 2`, live `4` — so preserving that reader would serve silence; the non-truncating Stop correctly installs the sealed take — `captureToken 4`, `rows 2`, ticks 192/288, emitted continuously with no foreign note row. DEC-141's term (`after.captureToken == before.captureToken`) therefore refused the healthy handoff and inspected only the first post-Stop sample, so it could pass the preserved empty window without requiring the take (its own `matched-fix-04`: first sample `rows 0`, sealed take on `obs[1]`). **DEC-144** makes it conditional: where the pre-Stop window was current, the same reader/token term stands and that sample must hold the take's rows; where it lagged live, the handoff must complete inside the observed sequence — some sample names the sealed generation and holds at least the take's rows. Fixtures `matchedStopServesTheSameTakeAcrossTheGenerationHandoff`, `matchedStopHandoffNamesTheSealedTakeOnly`, `truncatingStopDoesNotTakeTheMatchedTerminal` (focused **66/66**; full native **3,330 / 7 skipped / 3,323 succeeded / 0 failed**). Offline re-verification: the captured `captures/i5-3g-campaign-01/matched` now returns `matching_physical_reader_preserved`; `held`/`growth-empty` unchanged; the older matched runs still pass (sealed take on the second post-Stop sample), while host and synthetic controls refuse a sequence that never seals or seals without the rows (`scripts/test_rolling_record.py` 21/21). **No firmware change; the board stays on the rolling qualification image by owner instruction.** The device re-run campaign (`growth-empty-03` + `held-02` + `matched-fix-01`) aggregates to **`PASS`** (`full_recipe_complete: true`, `issues: []`, firmware `0b4b6fe2…`, commit `689ec471…`, `captures/i5-3g-campaign-01/aggregate-fix-02`). This is the **rolling Record route's** device acceptance, not a 6.4/3.15f/S4f.8 checkoff: 3.15f still requires every migrated route, 6.4 still owes its F-7/F-8/AC-8 hardware legs, and S4f.8 remains with RWO.

The first `growth-empty` attempt refused at the empty leg's scoped clear (`post_load_holdoff`); the same-boot retry (`growth-empty-02`) passed both legs. **`growth-empty` PASS** (`corrected_frozen_handoff` ×2) and **`held` PASS** (`corrected_frozen_root_return` — the DEC-136 frozen serving phase, root-backed Committed takeover and release, now proven by the registered oracle). The same run shows the refused-bind shape the native settlement fixture builds: `Deferred Record return bind refused slot=3; frozen source retained`, with the take still served. **`matched` FAIL:** a non-truncating Stop (`raw_length 560 → final_length 768`) did not preserve the physical reader — `(currentRole,currentStorage)` `(0,49)→(2,56)` and `captureToken` `32→34` (post-stop sample at tick 744, inside the same 768 cycle, so not the wrap-rotation artifact); the next frozen-token term would fail too. **Reading:** DEC-136's current-window progression serves a frozen window during recording, so the pre-stop served token lags live; a matching Stop seals at the newer generation and installs a new frozen reader — the DEC-138 matched terms predate that progression. **Oracle NOT edited** (no-weakening rule): owner decides between a DEC-136-aware matched terminal with a discriminating change and a route fix that preserves the reader. 6.4, 3.15f and S4f.8 stay open; no checkoff.
**2026-10-19 — I5 — 3.15g follow-up — the recorded DEC-136 frozen-token/live-copy risk is settled by native fixture (native GREEN; no firmware change, device NOT RUN).** The 3.15g checkoff recorded one bounded risk: a pre-seal **live** rolling copy carries the same capture token, so after a *refused* `bindFirstRecordingBar` it can pass as the frozen reader. Two registered cases in `test_midi_input_clock_integration` (`rolling_record_coverage.inc`) settle it by measurement: `refusedBindPreSealLiveCopyNamesTheSameTakeOnly` and its discriminating control `refusedBindUnextendedLiveCopyKeepsTheOlderToken`. **2026-10-19 — I5 — 3.15g — DEC-143 sealed-extent overlay: the merged fallback serves a published Record slice, and its source is now the object the decision protects (native + both builds green; device run owed).** The recorded next step was "hand the gather the presentation's sealed `rawRange`". `Loop::tryGatherPublishedSnapshotEventsInWindow`'s `RecordOverlay` branch now walks that extent as this Loop's own **read borrow** (keyed on the slot-owned `CaptureStopPresentation`, validated row by row by `CaptureRange::read` for generation, pool occupant and seal, so a recycled chunk can only stop the read), applies `projectRecordStopTick`, filters the half-open window, tick-sorts, and closes lanes left open **exactly once at the loop end only when the window is the loop** (a partial window's off may still be a later window). `passes.recordPass.committedChunkIds` is no longer a source. `ensurePlaybackMergedMidiEventsBuilt` states only the publication edge (`hasPublishedRecordPresentationForSlot` = `retirementActive` plus the runtime's presentation owner) and keys the reuse guard on the **extent's own address**, so the pre-edge empty build can no longer be served after the edge — the withdrawn form's exact failure — while an unchanged extent performs no gather. **Fixtures:** `test_loop_take_survival` gained a seal→borrow→commit fixture and four cases (withdrawn form's refusal control, wrapped-take projection + whole-loop-only closure, gather idempotence, undone pass refused); `test_rolling_record_retirement` gained `test_the_merged_fallback_serves_a_published_record_slice_before_its_root` on the production path (non-empty window at `RecordPublished` with no root, one rebuild, 16 no-op turns, one rebuild when the root publishes, no duplicate note). **Red-proved twice** (`false &&` on the Track predicate → only that case fails at "must not hold an empty window"; `false &&` on the Loop's overlay source → exactly the five serving cases fail with the refusal control green; both restored byte-identically). **One focused review's findings fixed and re-verified:** an incremental overdub admit keeps its wrap while the overlay serves (identity kept only in that window), an undone Record take is refused instead of re-served from its sealed extent (pass state, not publication state), a failed row read is a whole miss rather than a truncated window, and the negative half of the gate is covered. **Gates:** focused 356/356 across four suites; **2026-10-18 — I5 — the recorded `CaptureStopJob` split is falsified by the ring's own structure, and the harness wall now has numbers (measurement only; no production change, no checkoff).** Next step from the conflation diagnosis was RED 1 and then the "completed-slice / deferred-presentation" ring-role split (mark a `RecordPublished` job presentation-only *by phase*, and let the interaction gates consult "a slice-incomplete job is pending"). Read against the code, the design's step 2 — "release the job's interaction role synchronously" — is not expressible, for two independent reasons. **(1) The ring is serviced at its head only:** `Track::processDeferredOverdubStopGrain` binds `captureStopJobHead()` once for the whole grain and never re-resolves it, and its Record arm dispatches on `stop.phase`, so a successor admitted *behind* a presentation-only holder is never serviced and its slice can never close — freeing the interaction **gate** does not free the **service**. **(2) There is one finalizer role per slot, and the presentation obligation holds it:** the single `LoopPlaybackRuntime::captureStopOwner` is exactly what `hasBoundRecordReturnWindowForPendingJob()` (`captureStopOwner != nullptr && captureStopOwner->pending`) keys on, and with it the E2 frozen-reader route, the S7.5b.5 release edge and the DEC-136 hold; the same pointer denies both successor admissions (`beginDeferredRecordStopForSlot` → `finalizer_owner_held`; `beginDeferredOverdubStopForSlot` → that term beside `hasPendingDeferredOverdubStop()`). Handing the pointer to the successor re-keys the presentation and stops serving the frozen range; keeping it leaves the successor unreachable; a second per-slot role is a new field in a struct pinned at 7,880 B, and no re-base is authorized. **The harness wall is now measured, not asserted** (temporary probe, removed; suite back to its unchanged **14/14**): `loop.lastTickInLoop` is `UINT32_MAX` at the Record stop unless the slot is played across a wrap first, so `stepDeferredRecordRetirement`'s S7.5b.5 block is skipped and the job retires within 16 deferred turns (`pending=1, phase=16, queue=1, bound=1, lastTick=4294967295` → `pending=0, queue=0`); and once the loop *has* wrapped (`lastTick=608`, `pending=1, phase=16, bound=1, playing=1`), a live overdub served for two bars leaves `publishedPlaybackWindowForSlot` **false**, so the job retires again (`pending=0, served=0`). The board's held state (`retire_hold` **mask 239**: served = the job's frozen window, `recordReturnBound=1`, `pending=1, phase=16`) needs a **serving** frozen reader that survives an overdub start — that construction is RED 1's real prerequisite. **Decision owed before any production shape is chosen:** (A) a second per-slot presentation role — one EXTRAM pointer field in `LoopPlaybackRuntime` (no RAM1 effect) and a measured size-pin re-base; or (B) first make the harness able to build a serving frozen reader that survives an overdub start (test-only), so RED 1 and RED 2 exist first. **State:** no production line changed; focused `test_rolling_record_retirement` **14/14**; device untouched on the pinned default `08f43e45…`; no build, upload, SD or device action; no DEC; **6.4/3.15f/3.15g stay open**, 29/60. **2026-10-18 — I5 — the build-drop cycle is measured and has **no dropped build**: the stall's wait is upstream of every release site (instrumentation only; no production behaviour change, no checkoff).** Owner-approved route: instrument the job → `build+job` → `job` lifecycle, name the exact destroy/detach site and its reason, correlate by demand/root identity, and record whether the disappearing build published, transferred authority or made retryable progress. A `build_drop` row (on the existing `win_frozen_readiness` receipt, `#ifndef`-guarded — no new capture symbol, no RAM1 cost) now probes the builder at **all ten release sites** (`applyPlaybackViewTransition`, `cancelPlaybackLaunchForSlot`, `cancelRollingPlaybackWindow`, the three `retireCoverageSource` edges, both source-superseded `discardCoverageBuild` edges, the late-completion discard, the DEC-136 root-return hold expiry) **plus the two transitions no site owns**: `completed_unpublished` — `RuntimePlaybackViewBuild::active()` is false for `Phase::Complete`, so a finished build leaves the owner set with no release running — and `released_without_site`. The prior turn read this as "the failing term is the OTHER conjunct" only because the probe's format string had **no specifier for the `admitted` argument** (a `-Wformat-extra-args` warning on that very line), so the value was never displayed; the instrument is repaired and reports what it computes. The targeted record is also already null there: the refusal happens at `coveragePreparation=AwaitingAdmission`, where `activeViewBuildWork()` is gated off by `coverageBuildNeedsService()`, and the end state reads `buildActive=0 owned=0 pendingJudge=0`. **Proven blocker:** the declared service envelope charges `5 grains × (7+1) turns × 64 ticks = 2 560` plus the one-bar `leadTicks` 768 = **3 328 ticks of lead** for a demand on a **1 536-tick (2-bar)** take — more than a whole loop, so no interval of that take can ever be admitted as a root-backed window (even the smallest coverage demand needs 1 792 > 1 536). **2026-10-12 — I4 — Set browser empty root cause established read-only: the legacy SavedSet index clobbers the Set revision catalog index.** Owner-requested diagnosis of run02's *"actual SD cause UNKNOWN"*; no firmware/test/device/SD/upload/Git action. `/MidiLooper/sets/index.bin` has two owners in two layouts: `SetRevisionCatalog::writeSetCatalogIndex` writes a **16-byte** `SetCatalogIndex` there at commit `CatalogUpdate`, while the legacy SavedSet sequence index (`SavedSetCatalog::writeSetIndex` + `kSaveFileToken` `0x45564153` `"SAVE"`) writes **8 bytes** (4+4) to the same path via `writeSetIndexToSd` (they also share the temp path `sets/index.bin.tmp`). `BootRecovery::loadState` reconciles that path at **every boot with a current workspace** (`reconcileSetIndexOnSdWithOutcome`), and a catalog index is *never* legacy-readable (its token slot reads `reserved`+`nextSetId`, never `"SAVE"`), so the repair rewrite always fires and leaves the legacy 8-byte form. The browser entry then fails `readSetCatalogIndex` (16-byte read on an 8-byte file) → `listSetRevisionBrowserEntries` returns **0 rows** → `rootWorkspaceListRowCount` = 2 → the second scroll clamps at `Current` (run02 `OVLY,sel,0,1`, `cachedSetCount 0`). **Device evidence, already captured:** `[StorageManager] readRaw … Needed: 16, available: 8` right after `LDSV,1` and again at the Save-commit arm in `captures/i4-checkpoint-t8s4-02` and `-03` (whose COMPLETE wrote `S1 v2`), and right after `[INFO] Load/save mode entered` in run02; the 16-byte layout is `static_assert`ed and the Save/Current detail resolve is in-memory, so that read is the catalog index; `captures/i4-overlay-load-t8s4-01` has no such row but is **not** a discriminator (absent index or a gate-skipped refresh are silent too). **Contributing defect B (latent):** `loadSaveListCacheValid_` has no invalidation site and the refresh is attempted only on the overlay-enter transition, so a Set saved while the overlay is open cannot appear until reboot, and one skipped refresh leaves the browser empty for the whole session. **Named, not claimed:** the 8-byte file is a valid legacy index (not corruption), no revision payload is deleted by the rewrite, and both the set-id-reuse risk (`allocateNextSetId` defaults to id 1 on an unreadable index) and the silently skipped `queueWallClockSdCatalogSync` are unverified. Fix candidates and the fresh-boot acceptance criterion are recorded: ownership split (`sets/catalog.bin`) **plus a mandatory bounded rebuild of the catalog index from validated Set folders** — a read of the old path only helps a card whose catalog file is still intact, and an unreadable index must never resolve to the default id 1 (derive `max(setId)+1`); cache invalidation on publication plus a retry of a gate-skipped refresh; a browser folder-scan fallback is subordinate, never the substitute; and both index owners share their temp file too. One adversarial read-only review endorsed the cause and required that rebuild form of recovery plus tests for commit → boot reconciliation → browser listing, an already-clobbered card, an interrupted rebuild and no existing-revision overwrite. **Implementation is not authorized** by this diagnosis. [I4 — Set browser diagnosis](../../openspec/changes/runtime-working-set-ownership/evidence/2026-10-12-i4-ui-storage/SET-BROWSER-EMPTY-CATALOG-DIAGNOSIS.md).

**S7.5a — the first overdub's playback supply stalls ~2.8 s and then bursts the backlog (2026-10-11; device-side finding, measured on the authorized base leg; no fix, no limit, no checkoff).** Owner report while watching the run: during the first overdub nothing new appeared on the display and then the notes "burst". Measured from the device's own rows and reproducible (`captures/host-grid-record-t8s4-05`, after `…-t8s4-03` and `…-t8s4-01`; identical invocation, no upload, no flash): the outbound MIDI stream stops for **2837 / 2769 / 1446 ms** while carrying only **48 ticks (one grid step)** of musical time, then resumes at the very next grid step (tick **720 → 768**) and **flushes the backlog — 46 rows in 30 ms carrying ticks 768 → 1488** — before returning to real time; the display note count sits at 32-33 and then jumps to 47. Inside that gap the device is busy rather than hung: `DIAG,win_gap` **206** rows (one every 13.8 ms), `PERS` 89, `DIAG,snapshot_unit` 79, `DIAG,stop_grain` 35, `DIAG,lcr` 28, `DIAG,win_readiness` **13** (`owes_currency, window_rebuild`, ~200 ms cadence), `LED` 147, `MI,U` 37 — while `MO` (MIDI out) is **0** and `DISP`/`DFRAME` fall to 2 rows each; at the resume `DIAG,playback_build,snapshot,1448,0,1536,…` completes and `DIAG,late_route,144,8,0,0,54,0` records **max 0 µs** for the notes that did leave, i.e. the lateness is upstream of the MIDI route. **Discriminators:** the *second* overdub has no gap at all (first row +6 ms, zero `win_readiness`), and `…-t8s4-01` ran on the **previous commit** with the same signature — so this is not the run-end transport-gesture change, which `…-t8s4-05` re-confirms (`run_end_transport_stop=host_realtime_stop`, `transport_press_count=1`, record `1536/1536` `raw 1536`, `record_grid_first_note_tick=0`, shutdown `complete/2/ok`, no latch). **Folded into the same record (same class, different observation):** after an interrupted run left the board playing, an 8 s read-only attach found the firmware alive (`[Memory] ext` once per second, queries answered) with **zero** `DFRAME`/`DISP`/`#CAP` rows — a dark screen — restored immediately by the managed run's soft `!REBOOT` (no upload, no flash). **Lead, not a root cause:** the window supply of a sounding slot that is simultaneously carrying the previous take's finalization/persistence (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild` currency/build path; `LoopContentResolution`'s `lcr,srcskip,…reason=not_finished` at the gap start), with the confirmation path named in the packet. Packet: [FIRST-OVERDUB-SUPPLY-STALL.md](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-11-first-overdub-supply-stall/FIRST-OVERDUB-SUPPLY-STALL.md). **S7.5a — the host-grid record phase's follow-up: the run's *final* transport stop is the host's realtime `Stop`, and the record/overdub stops stay record-button presses (2026-10-11; host tooling only, no limit declared).** Owner direction: use MIDI `Stop` only at the end of the HITL test; a record stop or overdub stop is still handled via the MIDI buttons. **Landed:** `_run_end_transport_stop(out_port, *, master, press_ms)` at the run's single end-of-run site (`--stop-after-overdub`) — with the host owning the clock it calls the new `MidiClockMaster.send_realtime_stop()` (the `Stop` byte **without** retiring the pump: a transport stop is not a clock-source change, so the run-end drain keeps exactly the pacing condition the press-based stop produced; `stop()` stays the teardown shape, and pump retirement stays where it already was — the pre-arm `master.stop()` inside `_ensure_transport_stopped_before_record_arm` and the loop teardown); only the **last** leg owns the gesture (`is_final_leg`), so an earlier leg's stop in a multi-track run stays the button press, and the temporary `--post-save-play-wait-ms` replay branch writes `transport_press_after_replay` because it restarts the transport *after* this stop and returns `"host_realtime_stop"`; with no host master it presses `GLOBAL_TRANSPORT_NOTE` as before and returns `"transport_press"`. The gesture is recorded as `assertions.run_end_transport_stop`. **S7.5a — the host-grid record phase: the python script dictates tick 0, so the record stop lands on the requested bar (2026-10-11; host tooling only, no limit declared).** Executes the bounded next step the entry below names, and answers the owner's report that the base HITL's notes are "one bar too late, making the loop length 3 bars instead of 2". Two host-side pacing defects, both from not owning tick 0: **(a)** the base record phase emitted **no in-stream stop at all** (`_stream_pattern_for_bars` was called without `stop_press_note`, so its `stop_press_trigger_clock` stayed `None`) and the record press came afterwards from wall time — and the device acts on a MIDI button short press only when its double-tap window expires (`MidiButtonProcessor::onShortRelease`, 300 ms), i.e. `press_ms + 300 ms` after the note-on, while the committed length is the raw stop tick quantised to the **nearest bar** (`RecordStopLength::quantizeTransportRecordLength`, ± half a bar = 1000 ms at 120 BPM but 400 ms at 300) — so the same lateness fits at 120 BPM (why `envdist-t8s4-01` committed exactly 1536/1536) and mis-buckets at 300 (why `base-300bpm-preseam-probe-t8s4-07` and `base-300bpm-hostclock-after-intent-t8s4-03` both committed **2304/1536**); **(b)** in host mode the note stream was anchored on the host's *observation* of the device's serial `RECORDING` row instead of the realtime `Start` that produced tick 0, which is the measured 10–37-clock first-note offset. **Landed:** `MidiClockMaster.start()` retires any previous pump, sends the realtime `Start`, then records the grid origin pulse (the next pump pulse = **device tick 0**, per `ClockManager::onMidiStart`'s `assignCurrentTickSilently(0)` + `firstPulseAfterStart`) with `grid_origin_pulse()`/`tick_for_pulse()`; `stream_pattern_for_bars(..., grid_origin_pulse=…)` makes grid position 1 that pulse (grid position `c` → device tick `(c-1) * TICKS_PER_CLOCK`, so step 0 is tick 0 and step `s` tick `48s`), refuses a masterless/pumpless anchor by name, **degrades and reports** (`grid_anchor_missed_pulses`) instead of raising when the host already passed the anchor, does not consult the lagging device `BAR` probe in that mode, and reports `grid_origin_pulse`/`grid_first_note_pulse`/`grid_first_note_tick` so "the script dictated tick 0" is a **reading**; `record_stop_press_advance_clocks(bpm, press_ms)` converts the button lead into the clocks before the boundary at which the in-stream stop press must be emitted (20 clocks @120 BPM, 50 @300), so the effect lands on the boundary — the centre of the requested bucket; the base record branch anchors on the Start grid, refuses a missed anchor by name, takes its stop lead from `_host_grid_record_stop_advance_clocks` (a *smaller* explicit `--stop-press-advance-clocks` is raised to the button latency with a printed warning; one that cannot fit the phase is refused), presses in-stream on that grid, skips the serial `RECORDING` confirmation in host mode and **asserts it after the phase** from the rows the device emitted during it, `_restart_transport_after_clear`'s callers no longer apply the modelled button debounce to a realtime `Start`, and one `_record_phase_sent_its_own_stop` helper (per stream shape, reading each emitter's own statement) so the caller cannot press a second time on an already-`PLAYING` track. **What the anchor does *not* buy, stated rather than implied:** whenever the guard passes, the anchored origin equals the pulse the unanchored path would have used, so the schedule arithmetic is the same and the first-note win comes from removing the serial `RECORDING` wait; the anchor makes grid position 1 *provably* the tick-0 pulse (`grid_first_note_tick == 0`), turns a stalled host into a named refusal rather than a silent shift, and puts the stop press on the same grid as the notes. **Verified:** `scripts/test_hitl_host_grid_record.py` **19/19** (the real master's origin and tick mapping plus a second `Start` rebasing the grid; the arm anchor is the Start instant and not `press_ms + 300 ms` on *both* of its expression sites; step `s` on tick `48s`; the device `BAR` probe not consulted when anchored **and** still truncating when not — the control; masterless/pumpless anchors refused by name; a passed anchor degrading with no exception; the press lead as the button model in clocks; a caller lead inside that latency raised, one that cannot fit refused; the stop effect inside the ± half-bar bucket at 20/60/120/200/300 BPM; the press on the grid pulse the schedule names, exactly once; the composition reading every stream shape; plus a source-scan tripwire for the record phase's call sites); **six mutations** red-proved with byte-identical restores; full host sweep **1,426 tests / 6F+1E** = the pristine `3caa2bfb` set (1,407 tests, the same 6F+1E, re-run in a fresh `git worktree` for the A/B) plus exactly the 19 new tests, neighbours unchanged (`test_midi_clock` 18/18, `test_hitl_first_note_intent` 20/20). **One adversarial read-only review pass raised one blocker and three real defects, all repaired:** the past-anchor guard would have raised out of a take whose transport was already armed (now a degradation + a caller-side refusal), an explicit `--stop-press-advance-clocks` below the button latency re-created the one-bar take (now raised/refused), and the dropped `RECORDING` confirmation had no replacement (now asserted after the phase); **S7.5b.8b — the seed's killer was a host transport toggle read from a display frame; host fix verified and the seed now lands two bars (2026-10-10).** The "controlled seed/clock pacing diagnosis" the hardware journal owed is closed on the host side, and the rerun seed now commits the fixture. **Cause, measured on `captures/live-current-root-entry-t8s4-04`:** `_ensure_transport_stopped_before_record_arm` (`scripts/hitl/legacy_record_baseline.py`) read `_serial_sequencer_running` — whose marker list counts `#CAP,DFRAME`, the periodic display-frame monitor a **stopped** device keeps emitting every ~1.504 s — as proof of a running transport. Replaying the predicates against that session log truncated at the press gives `_transport_running_before_record_arm False` (the transport had been stopped since device 1590.044 s) with `_serial_sequencer_running True`; the live tail's only marker rows were two `DFRAME` rows. So the precondition pressed note 39 (`GLOBAL_TRANSPORT_NOTE`) at 1593.639576 on a stopped device, which **started** the transport (`Recording started @ tick 0` 1594.430), and `_restart_transport_after_clear` pressed the same toggle at 1594.630448 → `Transport stopped` 1595.165. The take ended at tick 384 with `length 768` (the 1-bar default) and one captured note whose off landed after the stop. **Fix:** `serial_lines_show_running_transport` (`scripts/hitl/serial_transport.py`) — the same device-time live window, counting only `,BAR,`/`,BPM,` — used by the precondition, with the post-stop re-check made **windowed** (`serial_global_transport_running(..., after_index=post_stop_baseline)`) so it cannot re-press on the stale evidence that authorized the press; `_TRANSPORT_MARKERS`/`serial_line_is_transport` keep their "is the link alive" meaning untouched. Replay of the failed seed's own prefix now presses nothing at any `after_index`, while the same capture's genuinely-running call still presses exactly once. **Authorized rerun** (clear/overwrite only track 8 / slot 4, no upload — HEX `9e8270b4…` unchanged): **1536 ticks / 2 bars** (`final_length_ok True`, was 768/False), **8 On + 8 Off with 0 unmatched** (was 1/0/unmatched 1), first note **2.626 ms / 0 clocks** (was 486 ms / 23), `record_clock_pulses_seen 192`, jitter 0.0, and stored `REVT` ticks exactly the canonical `EDIT_RECORD_FIXTURE` (`2,192,384,576,864,1056,1248,1344`) with the intended control-action sequence and no spurious transport press. **Named, not smoothed:** the base report's `overall_ok=false` is the host's 16th-grid expectation measured against a beat-and-seam fixture (inapplicable, skipped for `record_only`); and the leg itself still fails its own oracle — `selected_note_moved`, `stacked_reselect_after_deselect` (`move_index null`), with `Timed out waiting for stable select at tick 384 (±24)` — while `note_edit_entered` and `select_apply_highlight_follows` pass.
