**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 7: the grain-cost model, measured (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10; test-only).** The envelope 3.10 asked to derive is now derived from a measurement, not an assumption. Sweep (reading `nextCoverageBuildGrain()` before each turn): window events **1 and 10 → 1 turn with no order grain**; **20 → 11 orders / 12 turns**; **40 → 25 / 27**; **80 → 57 / 60**; **160 → 127 / 132**. Controls: the same 80 notes cost identically on a **32-bar and a 64-bar** loop, and the same 80 notes **spread** out of the window cost **one** turn — so cost is a function of the **window's event count alone**, with a **threshold near 10** and **super-linear** order work above it. Derived bound in the contract's currency (`turns × maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn`): 80 events = **46 080 ticks ≈ 60 bars** (fits a 64-bar loop, not a 32-bar one); 160 events = 101 376 (fits neither). **Contradictions now numeric:** the declared 7 grains (28-turn worst case) covers `N ≈ 5–10`, not 80; an admitted 80-event window on a 32-bar loop needs 46 080 ticks against the declared **29-bar lead**; `kWindowAdmissionLimit = 2048` extrapolates to ~1 600 lane turns ≈ 1 600 bars. **Preferred reconciliation (stated, NOT applied):** keep the grain quanta, derive the declared grain counts **and** 3.12's admitted window size from the measured envelope and the loop's length — high confidence the capacity is the wrong side, medium on the exact form; not applied because it moves the declared lead, 3.12's limit and 4.4's floor and would refuse shapes admitted today. **M98–M100** red-prove the fixture, M100 showing the derivation reads the **declared** field. Verified: 72/72, full native **2707 / 2700 / 7 / 0**, build SUCCESS (relink), RAM1 line **byte-identical**, **no re-base**. Evidence: [`evidence/2026-10-02-s310g-cost-model/EVIDENCE.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-02-s310g-cost-model/EVIDENCE.md).


**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 8: source-lifetime repair, holder-fairness repair, and the derived admission (not enabled) (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10).** This answers an independent review thread, and two of the three items were **defects in my own earlier increments**. **(1) Source lifetime.** `prepareOwingWindowHolder` gathered the request source into a **stack-local** `SessionMidiEventVec` while `RuntimePlaybackViewFill::step` reads `source_[cursor_]` **across turns** — so every turn after the helper returned read a dead frame. **The repair is what proves the review's point that this invalidated measurements: three fixtures' outcomes changed the moment the source became valid** (the composed fixture's completion count, the sparse window's 1 → 2 turns, and two cases of the urgency fixture turning out **unable to fail** — they passed only because the dangling source had made a slot stop owing — so they were removed, since an assertion that cannot fail is not evidence). The fix is a file-scope **per-slot** buffer: two slots can owe at once, and the caller owns the source for the build's whole duration. **(2) Holder fairness.** `selectPlaybackHolder` applied earliest-deadline-first **globally**, and my own doc even called that "the tighter of the two readings". The spec is explicit — *"Service SHALL **rotate round-robin across eligible holders**, and **within a holder** SHALL serve the earliest outstanding playback deadline first"*, with the scenario *"WHEN **a holder has more than one outstanding playback deadline**"* — and the design names the order: **"2 — Fairness, then deadline order."** The global form **starves**: a permanently-earlier deadline wins every rotation and the cursor cannot rescue the loser. Repair: **`selectPlaybackHolderRoundRobin`** is the across-holders rule, `selectPlaybackHolder` keeps the within-a-holder role with its doc corrected at the source, `src/main.cpp`'s track choice uses the round-robin form, and a new fixture drives the production composition with two tracks whose deadlines really are unequal and whose near obligation is long-lived (80 notes) — both are served within one rotation, where the old rule took every turn. **(3) The derived admission.** `applyWindowCostToContract` is now the single source of truth: `ceil(events / kPlaybackViewFillQuantum)` fills + `RuntimePlaybackOrderBuilder::requiredGrains(events, kPlaybackViewOrderQuantum)` order grains + one promotion grain. **The corrected cost model, measured with valid sources:** events = **2 × notes** (increment 7's column was notes), fills = **⌈events/64⌉ exactly**, and orders **equal the helper exactly where a merge runs** (11/25/57/127 for 40/80/160/320 events) while falling **below** it where the input is already ordered (20 events: bound 5, measured 1 — increment 7's "threshold near 10 events" was that skip, not a size threshold) — and increment 7's 2 048-event extrapolation (~1 600 grains) was simply wrong: the helper gives **982 order + 32 fill**. It is **implemented and deliberately NOT enabled**, for a measured reason: at the *declared* `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` and the rotation-derived gap, an 80-note window's derived need is ≈ **428 bars**, so enabling it refuses the shapes the current constants admit — the capacity reduction the review said not to approve on unmeasured evidence. **The service-gap bound is split honestly:** the **rotation** half is proven (the exact rotation sequence, plus the new fairness fixture), while the **ticks-per-turn** half is not — `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` remains the declared one bar, and the sweep fixture now asserts that as a statement so the envelope cannot be read as supported ("a supported deadline envelope still requires a proven service-gap bound — not merely larger constants"). *Verification:* `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` **73/73**; full native **2708 / 2701 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**; build **SUCCESS** from a **true rebuild** (82.6 s, cache cleared) with the RAM1 line **byte-identical** (`variables 96,192 / code 392,328 + padding 888`) and **no re-base**. Retention fires at the four "not now" refusals (`BuildInFlight`, `SuccessorAlreadyPrepared`, `TrackInterferenceBudgetExceeded`, `CannotCompleteBeforeHandoff`); the admission that accepts the demand **discharges it whole**; `ContractUndeclared`, `AdmissionRefused`, `NotServable`, `SourceUnavailable`, `SourceNotCurrent`, `WindowExceedsRetainedCapacity` and `NoRuntime` retain nothing, so retention is per refusal name rather than a blanket. **Coalescing** (DEC-108 §13(a)) keeps the **oldest outstanding deadline as one coherent position** — deadline, epoch, geometry, origin phase and origin stamp all from the promise it names — while the content (identity, interval, cost) follows the newest attempt, since a newer window may satisfy the older obligation; an unqualified re-attempt never overwrites a qualified demand. An epoch or geometry change **voids the position and never the obligation** (§13(c)) and is named by the reader; identity is **generation-qualified** (§13(d)) so a returning slot never revives an earlier operation, and a demand under the new generation starts a fresh record rather than inheriting the older deadline. A pending demand is deliberately **not** outstanding work, so the per-track budget does not charge a sibling for it. **Fixtures (5)**: retained-with-original-deadline + discharged-by-admission + the nothing-owed class; the demand owes no grain; coalescing keeps the oldest deadline; epoch/geometry invalidation; the generation change. **Red-proofs M120–M126**, each failing its own named assertion and restored byte-identically (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp e98595129187ceee`, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.cpp 35eec9683a0fdfd2`, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.h 2e50b234a0cce56c`). **Defects found by running it, mine and fixed:** the first `retainViewPendingRequest` read the retained record through an alias **after** replacing it, handing the coalesced promise the newest attempt's origin stamp with the oldest deadline (the O4 fixture caught the incoherence; every retained field is now read into a locals set first); a fixture precondition of mine asserted nothing; and the **host-ABI size pin was unreachable dead code** — it sat in the `#else` of a branch whose `#if` already required `__IMXRT1062__`, so the "host pin unchanged at 6,544" claims of earlier records described an assertion no compiler evaluated (measured on the clean previous tree the host object is **8,624 B**); it is live (native) from this slice and re-based on measurement. Image `89e4d0c1…` built, **not uploaded** — no device action and no device claim. **Owed:** **O8, the re-attempt** (increment 25 — re-issuing needs a gather buffer that outlives the build and the lane turn owns none, a RAM-shape decision, and the same gap the qualification calls blocker 1), a production requester, the permitted service-gap/overrun policy, enforcement activation (awaits `Delta-max`), `H x K`, the systematic sweep, the device leg. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 27: blocker 3's second half — the admitted deadline is serviced on the live path (and a review's correction of the first half is recorded).** A review of increment 26 (pasted into the session and **independently verified here**) showed that landing claimed too much: the permitted-gap comparison lives inside `#if defined(SESSION_CAPTURE) || defined(PIO_UNIT_TEST_NATIVE)`, so it is **capture-lane telemetry**, not live enforcement — the wording is corrected in this entry and in the `s310u` packet (Addendum 3), and the same review supplied the oracle for the half that was still missing. **Increment 27 lands that half**, adopting the review's six requirements verbatim: the promise the admission makes (`PlaybackViewAdmittedWork::deadlineTick`/`clockEpoch`) is now **read where it is kept** — `Track::serviceAdmittedDeadlineMisses(clock)` runs at the **top of every lane turn for every slot holding a live promise**, so a build that has **not finished** is judged too (R1: independent of completion, the case a completion-time check structurally cannot see); each traversal of the promised interval is counted **exactly once**, computed from the clock and keyed on the promise's own admission tick, with only the traversals that still change the policy accounted (R2); the promise is judged only in the **epoch it was qualified in**, so a reset, seek or re-projection claims nothing and **erases nothing**, and a new promise starts its own count on its own interval (R3); the service only accounts and reports — it publishes nothing, adopts nothing and rebuilds nothing, so the previous revision keeps serving for the missed traversal and a late arrival waits for an eligible boundary (R4); the accounting and the latch are **unconditional code**, with only the row behind the capture seam (R5: enforcement, not telemetry — red-proved natively by gating the accounting behind `SESSION_CAPTURE`); and the judgement is **never routed through `resolvePlaybackLag`**, whose `Current` outcome would otherwise mask a late arrival that happens to carry the wanted revision (R6 — the review's sharpest point). What one miss *means* stays in **one implementation** (`Track::noteMissedTraversalForSlot`: the allowance `one_pass_late`, then the named `lag_breach` plus the latch), which `advancePlaybackLagTraversal` now also calls, so the revision rule and the deadline rule share one notion of a miss and differ only in what they judge; the deadline is **never re-positioned**. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 28: a review's three correctness gaps in the deadline service are closed, and containment is proved rather than counted.** A read-only review of increment 27 (pasted into the session and **independently verified here at `5cbd3bb8`**) confirmed three gaps and one unproven claim, all real. **(1) Request deduplication had become fault history.** `serviceAdmittedDeadlineMisses` called `lagState.resetEpisode(...)` whenever `admittedTick` changed, so a repeated request for the **same interval** minted a fresh first-miss allowance — exactly what DEC-108 §13(a) forbids (*"a later edit never resets an earlier interval's missed-deadline allowance"*). Now the per-promise traversal count still starts at zero (that *is* the deduplication) while the **episode** is reset only when the *interval* changes (`coversInterval(handoffPhase, admittedIntervalLength)` guards the call), so the interval's second miss is the named breach instead of another allowance. **(2) An epoch mismatch was skipped, not revalidated.** The service `continue`d silently, and publication had no clock-validity step. §13(c) says a changed clock invalidates the *promise*, never the content, and that the miss **is reported**: the mismatch now names `promise_epoch_invalidated` **once per promise** (per-slot `invalidatedPromiseTick`), claims no traversal miss, leaves the interval's history untouched, and retains the obligation **unmodified** (same admission tick, same deadline) so returning to that clock judges *that* promise again — so an epoch change can never mint an allowance. The content still publishes, which is **asserted**, not assumed. **(3) A deadline crossed at/around the final grain escaped.** The turn's clock is read *before* the worker grain and `activeViewBuildWork()` returns null the moment the build completes, so a build finishing a tick late was never judged. The promise is now **retained through completion** (`completedPromisePendingJudgement`, consumed by the next opportunity's fresh clock, and **cleared by a new admission** so a successor can never be judged as its predecessor). **(4) The review's closing point — *"accounting plus a latch does not yet prove late-publication containment"*** — is now a fixture: after the breach, `containmentForSlot(slot, phase)` reads `ContinuityContainment::ServeLastCoherentRevision` while coverage remains, so the policy is **read by containment**, not merely counted. **Fixtures (3, ownership suite):** the repeated-request + containment fixture (the successor promise's miss is the interval's second — named `lag_breach`, latch set, `one_pass_late` still 1); the real-epoch-change fixture (named once, no traversal count moved, obligation retained and re-judged on the return leg, the build **completes in the new epoch** and publishes, and a promise admitted in that epoch that misses is the **breach**); and the completion fixture (finished *inside* the promise, the record then unreadable, and the next opportunity past the deadline still names `one_pass_late` — once). **MC1-MC6** red-prove each behaviour (always reset the episode; skip the naming; reset on the mismatch; drop the retention gate; drop the retention record; never latch on the second miss) with every restore byte-identical (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp` **377b5041b44a8f9d** before and after each case; final **6f4961ef38d9186c** after the doc comments, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.h` **c9b5654c266b5138**). Two corrections were recorded rather than smoothed: the epoch fixture's first draft asserted an absolute `one_pass_late == 0` where its own earlier turn legitimately counted the allowance (now a *no-move* comparison), and the retention is a bool cleared at admission rather than a `tick != 0` sentinel, because tick 0 is a legal instant. Verified: focused **97/97** (94/94 at increment 27), full native **2,740 / 2,733 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, build **SUCCESS** with the RAM1 line byte-identical (`variables 96,192`, code 390,472 + padding 2,744) and one measured size re-base (target 6,816 -> **6,832** B, host 8,768 -> **8,784** B), `git diff --check` clean, `openspec validate --strict` valid. No upload and no device claim. **The review's verdict stands where it is about operation:** on the device the service still judges nothing (no production requester, the lane's production builds carry `clockEpoch == 0`, `sInterferenceBudgetEnforced` off), so blocker 3's operational half remains the production requester's qualified clock stamp.
